description: Sync issues, merge requests and their notes, Markdown files, releases, project descriptions and commit messages from the GitLab projects you choose. Private-project restrictions need Enforce ACL and readable member emails.
opening: Sync issues, merge requests and their notes, Markdown files on the default branch, releases, project descriptions and commit messages from the GitLab projects you select. Each issue, merge request, note, file, release, project and commit is one document, and a note links to its issue or merge request.

A private project's items are limited to its members only when Enforce ACL is on and HydraDB can read every member's email. Confidential issues and internal notes are kept only as empty placeholders. Code and diffs are not synced, and items deleted in GitLab stay in HydraDB.

permissions.who_can_read: Access follows the project. A public or internal project can be read by everyone who can query the collection. A private project can be read by its active members at any access level, including inherited group members and members of groups the project is shared with. A confidential issue, or an internal or confidential note, is kept only as a placeholder with no content, and with Enforce ACL on no one can read it.
permissions.identity: A member's email address, from the member list when GitLab shows it, else from the member's public profile email.
permissions.when_unreadable: If a member's email is hidden, the member list is incomplete, there are too many members to express, or no member can be expressed, the connector reports a permission warning for the whole project.
notes: Most GitLab users hide their public email, so a private project often needs an access rule you set.
Visibility of single issues is not reproduced, apart from confidential issues.
A project GitLab reports as not found may be deleted, or the token may have lost access. HydraDB does not treat it as deleted.

connect.auth: GitLab uses a personal, project or group access token with `read_api`.

settings.name: api_url
settings.text: The API address of a self-managed GitLab, including `/api/v4`, for example `https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4`. Leave it empty for GitLab.com. Self-managed GitLab is not yet a supported setup.

permissions.name: read_api
permissions.text: reads projects, issues, merge requests, notes and repository files, and a private project's members for permissions.

steps.title: Create a token
steps.text: Create a GitLab access token with `read_api` for a user who is a member of every project you will select.

steps.title: Create the connector
steps.text: Paste the token as `private_token`. For self-managed GitLab, set `api_url`.

steps.title: Select projects
steps.text: HydraDB lists the projects the token's user is a member of, up to 2,000. Select the projects to sync.

connect.account: One connector reads the projects one token's user is a member of.

sync.first_sync: Reaches back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default. Issues and merge requests are measured by last update, commits by creation and projects by last activity. Markdown files on the default branch can come across even when their last commit is older than the window.
sync.changes: Each sync reads issues and merge requests updated since the last sync, new commits and active projects. When an issue or merge request changes or gets a new comment, all its notes are read again. Markdown files are read again when the default branch gets a commit inside the window. A project with no recent activity can be skipped, releases included.
sync.edits: An edited issue or merge request updates its document. An edited note, or a note made internal, updates only when its issue or merge request changes or gets a new comment. An issue made confidential is replaced by its placeholder only when it is read again. Resetting the default branch to an older commit can leave newer file content in HydraDB.
sync.deletes: Issues, merge requests, notes and files deleted in GitLab stay searchable in HydraDB.
notes: A commit that appears in several selected projects is one document, attributed to the project read last.
Markdown files larger than 512 KiB are skipped, and reading a repository stops after 100,000 entries.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.gitlab_project_id
shared_attributes.text: The numeric project id. Limits a query to one project. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's items. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: Project
shared_attributes.text: The selected project. Its readers decide who can read every item in it. Not searchable.

documents.name: Issues and merge requests
documents.one_document: One issue or one merge request. Its notes are separate documents.
documents.title: The title. An item with no title is called `GitLab issue` or `GitLab MR` with its id. A confidential issue is titled `Confidential GitLab issue`.
documents.text: The description, else the title, then `Author` and `Assignees` lines, and for a merge request `Reviewers` and `Branch` lines. Labels are written as a `Labels` line and the creation time as a `Created` line. The title and the item id are searchable too. A confidential issue's text is a fixed placeholder sentence.
documents.date: When the item was last updated, else when it was created.
documents.link_back: The issue or merge request page on GitLab. Confidential placeholders have none.

attributes.name: Item id
attributes.text: `<project id>!<number>` for an issue and `<project id>!mr<number>` for a merge request. Keeps later syncs on the same document, also when an issue becomes confidential, and a search can match it.

attributes.name: labels
attributes.text: Label names, written as the `Labels` line.

attributes.name: author
attributes.text: The opener's username, written as the `Author` line. Not attached to the item as a person in the graph.

attributes.name: assignees
attributes.text: Assignee names, written as the `Assignees` line. Not attached to the item as people in the graph.

attributes.name: reviewers
attributes.text: A merge request's reviewer names, written as the `Reviewers` line.

attributes.name: source_branch, target_branch
attributes.text: A merge request's branches, written as the `Branch` line.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the item was created, written as the `Created` line. The result date when there is no update time.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the item was last updated. Not searchable.

attributes.name: mentions
attributes.text: Each `@username` in the description, recorded as a person the item mentions. The field itself is not searchable, but the description it comes from is.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.gitlab_iid
attributes.text: The issue or merge request number within its project. Combine it with `additional_metadata.gitlab_project_id` to pick out one item. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.gitlab_redacted
attributes.text: True on a confidential issue's placeholder. Finds placeholders. Not searchable.

attributes.name: state
attributes.text: `opened`, `closed`, `locked` or `merged`. It is not part of the text, so a query cannot match the state.

attributes.name: closed_at, merged_at
attributes.text: When the item was closed or merged.

documents.name: Notes
documents.one_document: One note on an issue or merge request. System notes, such as state and label changes, are left out. An internal or confidential note is kept as a placeholder with no content.
documents.title: `Comment on` with the parent's id. A placeholder is titled `Comment on a confidential GitLab issue`. The title is not searchable.
documents.text: The note text, with its author, its creation and update times and its parent's id. A placeholder's text is a fixed sentence.
documents.date: When the note was last updated, else when it was created.
documents.link_back: The note on its issue or merge request page.

attributes.name: author
attributes.text: The note author's username, else name. The graph records the note as written by this person.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: The issue or merge request the note belongs to, written as the `Parent` line. Links the note to it.

attributes.name: thread_id
attributes.text: Groups every note on one issue or merge request into one thread. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created_at, updated_at
attributes.text: When the note was created and last updated. The update time, else the creation time, is the result date.

attributes.name: mentions
attributes.text: Each `@username` in the note, recorded as a person the note mentions. The field itself is not searchable, but the note text is.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.gitlab_note_id
attributes.text: The note id. Picks out one note. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.gitlab_noteable_type
attributes.text: `Issue` or `MergeRequest`. Keeps only issue notes or only merge request notes. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.gitlab_iid
attributes.text: The parent's number within its project. With `additional_metadata.gitlab_project_id`, returns every note on one issue or merge request. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.gitlab_redacted
attributes.text: True on a placeholder note. Finds placeholders. Not searchable.

attributes.name: discussion_id
attributes.text: The GitLab discussion the note belongs to. Notes in one discussion are not linked as replies to each other.

attributes.name: path, line
attributes.text: The file and line a diff note was left on.

documents.name: Markdown files
documents.one_document: One non-empty Markdown file, `.md` or `.mdx`, on the default branch, up to 512 KiB.
documents.title: The file's first heading, else its file name without the extension.
documents.text: The file content. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: The time of the default branch's latest commit when the file was read.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.gitlab_project_path
attributes.text: The project path, for example `acme/backend`. Limits a query to one project by path. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.gitlab_path
attributes.text: The file path in the repository. Picks out one file. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.gitlab_blob_sha
attributes.text: The content hash of the file version read. Picks out one exact version. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.gitlab_ref
attributes.text: The branch the file was read from. Not searchable.

attributes.name: path, format
attributes.text: The repository path, and whether the file is `md` or `mdx`.

documents.name: Commits
documents.one_document: One commit. A commit that appears in several selected projects is one document.
documents.title: The commit title, else the first line of the message, else `GitLab commit` with its short id.
documents.text: The commit message, then an `Author` line. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the commit was created, else committed, else authored.

attributes.name: author
attributes.text: The author's name, written as the `Author` line. Not attached to the commit as a person in the graph.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the commit was created. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.gitlab_sha
attributes.text: The commit hash. Picks out one commit. Not searchable.

documents.name: Releases
documents.title: The release name, else `Release` with its tag.
documents.text: The release notes, else the title. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the release was published, else when it was created.

attributes.name: released_at, created_at
attributes.text: The publish time, else the creation time, is the result date. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.gitlab_tag_name
attributes.text: The release's Git tag. Picks out one release. Not searchable.

attributes.name: tag_name
attributes.text: The release's Git tag.

documents.name: Projects
documents.title: The project name with its namespace, else its path, else its name.
documents.text: The project description, else the title, then `Path` and `Topics` lines. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: The project's last activity, else when it was created.

attributes.name: path
attributes.text: The path with its namespace, written as the `Path` line.

attributes.name: created_at, last_activity_at
attributes.text: The last activity, else creation, is the result date. Not searchable.

attributes.name: default_branch
attributes.text: The project's default branch.

attributes.name: visibility
attributes.text: `private`, `internal` or `public`. Who can read the project's items is worked out from its members, not from this value.

example_searches: What did reviewers say on the merge request that changed the payment retry logic?
What does the README of acme/backend say about local setup?

connections: A note to its issue or merge request, with all notes on one item grouped into one thread.
A placeholder note to its confidential issue.
Notes in one GitLab discussion are not linked as replies to each other.
References such as `#12` or `!34` are not turned into links, and merge requests are not linked to the issues they close.
No links to items in other tools.
people: Each `@username` mentioned in an issue, merge request or note.
Issue and merge request authors, assignees and reviewers, and commit authors, appear only in the text.
graph.from_text: Issue, merge request, note, file, commit and release text.

not_synced: Projects the token's user is not a member of.
The content of confidential issues and internal notes. Only empty placeholders are kept.
System notes, such as state and label changes.
Code and diffs. Commits carry only their message, and only Markdown files are read.
Pipelines, jobs, branches, tags, wikis, snippets, and label and milestone lists.
Issue due dates, weights, time tracking, milestones and epics.
Commit statistics and author and committer emails.
Markdown files over 512 KiB, empty files, and files beyond the first 100,000 repository entries.
